content.comment_body: Hello, I was also waiting for MQTT support. It seems my modules need to be updated. After some practice, I managed to upgrade my [product_name] engineering software [version_no] on my old laptop. Currently, I have three older modules installed for several years: - [article_no] with firmware [version_no] - [article_no] with firmware [version_no] - [article_no] with firmware [version_no] These modules are quite old ([version_no]). I'm unsure if upgrading the firmware will make them work with the newer engineering software version. Most likely, I'll need to purchase three new modules. Additionally, I have a question about my extension modules: I have added an extension module with serial number [article_no]: [url] This module is discontinued, but will it be compatible with the new [version_no] modules? Thanks!

Modules manufactured before [version_no] cannot have their firmware updated. Updates are limited to the same series, for example from [version_no] to a later patch in that series, but not to a newer version. If you wish to use MQTT, you will need to purchase the latest [product_name] module with [version_no]. Expansion modules with order numbers ending in [article_no] or [article_no] are incompatible with [version_no]. Only modules with order numbers ending in [article_no] are supported.
Alright, thank you for your response.

Hello, I have another question. In my current setup using the older modules, I also have a compact switch module: [url] I cannot find a suitable replacement. Is it still acceptable to use this module? Thank you! [user_name]
The successor for that module is [article_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users face compatibility challenges when upgrading to newer software and hardware modules for [product_name] controllers. New features such as MQTT support require the latest versions of engineering software and hardware, leaving older modules (like those from [version_no] series and certain extension modules) unsupported due to firmware and hardware constraints. There is also uncertainty about using discontinued complementary modules, such as legacy switch modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek a simple upgrade process enabling use of new software features on their existing hardware, or clear guidance on which hardware remains compatible and what replacements are available for discontinued modules.
